Help, About & Privacy

Welcome to ClinBridge

Free Cardiac Health Tracking
Built by a cardiac patient, for cardiac patients. No account, no subscription, no ads — ever. Your data never leaves your device.
clinbridge.clinic
Scan to open ClinBridge on any device
What ClinBridge does

ClinBridge logs your blood pressure, heart rate, weight, fluid intake, symptoms, medications, meals, and activities — then analyzes the patterns over time so you and your cardiologist have real evidence to work from, not just a single office reading.

The app's four Advanced Analytics detectors continuously watch for clinically meaningful changes: sustained heart rate shifts, decompensation warning signs, pulse pressure trends, and symptom convergence patterns. When they find something significant, they tell you what was found and why it matters — in plain language.

⚠️ Important — What ClinBridge is not

ClinBridge is a pattern awareness tool, not a diagnostic device. It does not diagnose, prescribe, or replace your care team. All findings are described as directional — they point toward patterns worth discussing with your cardiologist, never toward a conclusion. The phrase you will see throughout the app: "Math is directional, not definitive."

What's in this app
📊 HR Rate Detector

Monitors 5 clinical signs of fluid overload building before a crisis

Getting Started — Why Settings Come First

ClinBridge is not a generic health app — it is a precision monitoring tool that adapts to your specific conditions, your doctor's targets, and your daily schedule. None of that happens automatically. Settings are where you tell ClinBridge who you are and what you need. Until Settings are filled in, the app operates on generic defaults that may not reflect your care plan at all.

⚙️ Step 1 — Open Settings before logging anything

Tap Settings on the main screen. Work through each section top to bottom. This takes about 3 minutes and unlocks the full power of ClinBridge.

👤 Patient Profile

Enter your name and date of birth. These appear on every exported report, PDF, and spreadsheet — so your cardiologist, nephrologist, or any specialist can immediately identify the record as yours. Without this, reports are anonymous and may be rejected by a medical office.

Select your cardiac conditions. This is not just a label — ClinBridge uses your condition profile to decide which warnings to surface, which patterns to flag in Advanced Analytics, and how to frame your data in the Doctor's Report. For example, if Postprandial Hypotension is selected, the app specifically tracks BP drops after meals and calculates your improvement percentage over time. If AFib is selected, heart rate variability and irregularity notes gain prominence in your reports.

⚙️ App Settings — Your Personal Target Ranges

These four ranges are the most important numbers in ClinBridge. Ask your cardiologist for your personal targets — they differ from textbook normals for most cardiac patients.

  • Systolic Range — Every BP reading is evaluated against this. Readings outside range are flagged with a ⚠️ warning dot on charts and counted in your out-of-range summary for doctor reports.
  • Diastolic Range — Same as above for the lower number. Both are shown side by side in Advanced Analytics so your cardiologist sees the full picture at a glance.
  • Heart Rate Range — Readings outside this window trigger alerts and are highlighted on the HR trend chart. Critical for patients on beta-blockers or with bradycardia/tachycardia history.
  • Daily Fluid Range (oz) — ClinBridge tracks your cumulative fluid intake throughout the day and shows a progress bar. When you approach your maximum, the app warns you. For CHF and kidney patients this setting is as important as BP.

📋 Tracking Features

Turn on only the features your doctor has prescribed. Enabling all features when you only need two creates noise. Each toggle you enable adds a tracking button on the main screen and unlocks a corresponding chart in Advanced Analytics.

  • ⚖️ Weight Monitoring — Tracks daily weight with automatic change alerts. CHF patients typically weigh daily; a gain of 2–3 lbs in 24 hours can signal dangerous fluid retention before symptoms appear. Set your alert threshold to match your cardiologist's instructions.
  • 💊 Symptom Tracking — Log dizziness, fatigue, chest discomfort, shortness of breath, and more. Symptoms are timestamped and correlated with BP readings in the Doctor's Report — giving your cardiologist context they cannot get from numbers alone. When your cardiac conditions are set in Settings, condition-specific symptoms appear automatically — for example, CHF patients see Cardiac Cough, Orthopnea, and Paroxysmal Nocturnal Dyspnea in their selector without having to add them manually.
  • 🏃 Physical Activity — Log exercise type and duration. Activity directly affects BP readings; logging it lets the app and your doctor distinguish exertion-related readings from true trend changes.

📅 Daily Schedule & Events

This is where ClinBridge becomes proactive rather than reactive. Create events for medication times, pre-meal BP checks, fluid targets, and any other recurring action in your care plan. At the scheduled time, ClinBridge fires an alert — on screen, with a chime, and with action buttons that let you log directly from the alert. No more missed readings. No more forgotten medications.

Each event can be set to fire on specific days of the week only — for example, a Sunday-only weekly backup reminder, or a Monday/Wednesday/Friday weigh-in event. Leave all days unchecked for daily firing (the default).

Event notifications can include a 💾 Backup Now action button — one tap saves your full backup file instantly from the notification without closing it, so you never forget your weekly backup.

For Postprandial Hypotension patients: set a pre-meal event 15 minutes before each meal with a fluid reminder. ClinBridge will prompt you to hydrate, then prompt you to take a BP reading before eating — the protocol that has been shown to reduce PPH episode severity.

🔔 Notifications

Enable OS notifications so event alerts reach you even when ClinBridge is not the active screen. On iPhone, the in-app alert always works when ClinBridge is open. For background alerts, install ClinBridge to your Home Screen via the Safari Share button.

📋 What your doctor gets from a well-configured ClinBridge
  • A timestamped BP trend over weeks or months — not just the reading taken in the office
  • Out-of-range readings flagged with context: what you were doing, how you were feeling
  • Medication effectiveness scoring based on BP patterns before and after dose times
  • Fluid intake correlated with weight changes — critical for diuretic management
  • PPH episode frequency and severity over time with percentage improvement
  • A exportable PDF or spreadsheet formatted for a medical record
The bottom line: A 3-minute investment in Settings transforms ClinBridge from a log book into a clinical-grade monitoring tool that speaks your doctor's language.

How to Use

Daily Workflow — 5 minutes or less
  1. Morning Check-In — Tap the yellow banner at the top each morning. 45 seconds. Records how you feel and yesterday's context for pattern tracking.
  2. Log BP — Use the Log Blood Pressure button after taking your reading. Tag it to a medication or activity if relevant.
  3. Log Fluid — Every time you drink something, tap Log Fluid or use the event buttons. The progress bar updates in real time.
  4. Log Meds — Mark each scheduled medication as taken when you take it. ClinBridge tracks adherence automatically.
  5. Events fire as reminders — Set up timed events in Settings (Morning Meds, Lunch, Evening Walk, etc.) and the app will prompt you at each one.
Before a Doctor Appointment
  1. Open Advanced Analytics — set the date range to cover since your last visit.
  2. Tap Generate Doctor's Report — reviews BP trends, medication adherence, symptoms, fluid behavior, and morning patterns in one printable document.
  3. Bring the report or show it on your phone/tablet during the appointment.
Keeping Your Data Safe
  1. Set up a weekly backup event in Settings — it will remind you every week and let you export with one tap from the notification.
  2. Use Device Sync & Backup → Export ALL Data before updating the app or switching devices.
  3. If you use ClinBridge as a Home Screen icon on iPhone — always export before deleting the icon, as removing it erases all local data.
Tips
  • Turn features on/off in Settings based on what your doctor has asked you to track.
  • Set your BP target ranges in Settings so the app can color-code readings correctly.
  • The Fluid Budget Dashboard lets you allocate your daily fluid goal across events so you pace intake throughout the day.
  • Log symptoms with a severity rating — the Doctor's Report uses this to flag high-severity episodes for your cardiologist.
  • Activity Timer: Use the timer in Log Activity to time workouts in real time. Tap ⏸ Pause to freeze the clock if interrupted — a PAUSED label confirms it's stopped. Tap ▶ Resume to continue, then ⏹ Stop & Use to save the full elapsed time.
  • HR Rate Detector — Quick Stats: Open HR Rate Detector and use the Today / 7 Days / 30 Days / All Time buttons to analyse your heart rate trends across any time window. The chart scrolls horizontally for multi-day views and shows date labels so you can pinpoint when patterns occurred.
  • Viewing history for any card: Each main page card (Blood Pressure, Weight, Symptoms, Activities, Meals, Medicines) has a 📋 View History button in its header. Tap it to see up to 90 days of entries in that card only — no other cards are affected. Tap ← Back to Today inside the card to return. Only one card can show history at a time.
  • Correcting past weight entries: Tap ✏️ Edit Past Entries on the Weight card header to open 90-day weight history. A 🗓️ Jump to date picker lets you navigate directly to any date. Entries that deviate significantly from your 7-day rolling average are automatically flagged — yellow ⚠️ for 10–19 lbs off, red 🚨 for 20+ lbs — so data entry errors are easy to spot without scrolling through every record.
📊 Advanced Analytics — The Four Detectors
These run on your historical data and identify patterns that are easy to miss in daily readings.
📊 HR Rate Detector

Analyzes your full HR history to find level shifts — periods where your resting heart rate durably changed to a new baseline — and rapid changes — sudden single-session jumps. Requires 6+ days of HR readings. Use the Today / 7 Days / 30 Days / All Time buttons to narrow the window. A "🔍 Investigate" button on any finding opens Anchor Date Investigation for that exact date.

🚨 Decompensation Warning

Monitors five clinical signals simultaneously: weight gain, cardiac output (HR + pulse pressure), symptom frequency, fluid intake patterns, and notes keyword scan. Each signal is scored individually. The composite result ranges from ✅ All Clear → 📋 Early Indicator (1 signal) → ⚠️ Monitor Closely (2+ signals) → 🚨 Contact Cardiologist (multiple red signals). One signal alone is not cause for alarm — the value is in seeing multiple signals converge.

🩺 Pulse Pressure Detector

Pulse pressure is systolic minus diastolic BP. Normal range is 40–60 mmHg. A narrowing trend can indicate the heart is working harder to maintain output; a widening trend may indicate arterial stiffness. Many cardiac patients have a chronically reduced PP that is their personal baseline — the detector recognizes this and labels it "Chronically Narrow — Your Stable Baseline" rather than an acute alert. What matters is change from your baseline, not comparison to a textbook number.

🔍 Symptom Convergence

Analyzes 30 days of symptom logs across three layers: (1) Intraday clusters — 3+ symptoms within a 4-hour window on the same day; (2) Multi-day escalation — the same symptom worsening in severity across multiple days; (3) Clinical triads — recognized symptom combinations with known cardiac significance (e.g., shortness of breath + fatigue + edema). The 60-day Timeline tab shows where clusters occurred visually.

📌 Pinned Events — Your Cardiologist Preparation Tool

When any detector finds a significant event (yellow or red), it suggests pinning it. Pinned events are saved permanently — they never roll off with the 90-day data window. Each pin captures the detector's full finding plus all raw log data for that date.

Pinned events appear in three places: the 📌 Pinned Events button in Analytics, the 60-day Timeline as amber markers, and your Doctor's Report as a dedicated section.

After your cardiologist appointment: use "Archive & Clear" to permanently save the current pins and start fresh for the next period. An appointment nudge reminds you automatically.

⚠️ About accuracy — read this once

All four detectors use statistical pattern detection on self-reported data. The math is directional, not definitive. A finding means: "this pattern is present in your data and worth discussing." It does not mean: "something is wrong." Findings can reflect real clinical changes, data entry errors, device variability, or normal day-to-day fluctuation. Your cardiologist provides the clinical interpretation — ClinBridge provides the data and the pattern recognition to make that conversation more productive.

🌡️ Heat & Humidity Advisory

Why Heat Matters for Cardiac Patients

Your heart already works harder than most. In hot weather, it must also pump extra blood to your skin to cool your body — on top of whatever activity you're doing. This dual demand can trigger dangerous drops in blood pressure, arrhythmias, or acute decompensation, especially with conditions like heart failure, hypertension, or a pacemaker/ICD.

How It Works
1. Log an activity — an optional Outdoor Temperature (°F) field appears in the activity log modal.
2. ClinBridge checks — if the temperature meets or exceeds your advisory threshold and you have heat-sensitive conditions in your profile, an advisory appears after saving.
3. Manual check — use the Run Manual Heat Check button in Settings → Heat & Humidity Advisory to preview an advisory for any temperature without logging an activity.
Heat-Sensitive Conditions Detected

ClinBridge automatically matches conditions in your profile against a list of cardiac and metabolic conditions known to increase heat risk: Heart Failure, Hypertension, Atrial Fibrillation, Coronary Artery Disease, Pacemaker/ICD, Cardiomyopathy, PAD, Diabetes, CKD, COPD, Obesity. Any custom conditions you've entered are also included.

Protective Strategies
  • Pre-hydrate: drink 8–16 oz of water before going outdoors
  • Avoid peak heat hours: 10 AM – 4 PM
  • Cool down for at least 10 minutes after exercise before re-entering an air-conditioned space
  • Watch for warning signs: dizziness, excessive sweating, flushing, rapid or irregular heartbeat, chest discomfort
  • Inform your cardiologist of any new symptoms that appeared during or after heat exposure
Disclaimer: Heat advisories are educational reminders, not medical diagnoses. Your cardiologist sets the final guidance on exercise and heat exposure for your specific situation.

🌅 Morning Check-In & Pattern Tracking

The Problem This Solves

When your doctor says "50 oz of fluid per day," they're giving you a safe baseline number — typically set for your average conditions. They're usually not accounting for your activity level that day, how many hours you'll be awake, whether it's hot outside, or how well you slept the night before. Your body's actual fluid needs vary with all of these things.

ClinBridge can't tell you whether to exceed your limit. But it can track what happens when you do — and over time, build a pattern that you and your doctor can review together to get you a more personalized recommendation.

How It Works

1. Each morning, a 45-second check-in prompt appears on your dashboard.
You tap how you feel (Good / Fair / Rough), note any morning symptoms, and answer a few quick questions about yesterday.

2. The questions focus on yesterday's context — were you physically active? Hot outside? Did you exceed your fluid limit? How did you sleep? Did you eat late?

3. After 7+ days of check-ins, the Doctor's Report gains a new section: Lifestyle & Recovery Patterns. This shows whether you felt better or worse the morning after over-limit fluid days, whether activity is a compensating factor, and how poor sleep affects your next-day symptoms.

4. You bring this report to your cardiologist. Instead of asking "can I drink more on busy days?", you show them 60 days of evidence — and they can give you an informed, personalized answer.

What Gets Tracked
Morning feeling
😊 Good · 😐 Fair · 😟 Rough
Morning symptoms
Swelling, fatigue, breath, fog, heaviness
Yesterday's activity
Active or not, heat exposure
Fluid vs. limit
Over / Within / Under your daily limit

Good or poor — correlates with BP
Waking hours

Where You See the Results
Doctor's Report → Lifestyle & Recovery Patterns section
After 7+ check-ins in the selected period, the Doctor's Report automatically includes pattern analysis — fluid over-limit correlation, sleep impact, top recurring symptoms, and a clinical note for your doctor. Under 7 check-ins, the section shows a placeholder explaining the feature to your doctor.
Advanced Analytics → Morning Patterns panel
Updated in v9.6.5. After 5+ check-ins, the Morning Patterns panel shows feeling distribution, fluid over-limit correlation, sleep quality impact, and top recurring symptoms. New in v9.6.5: symptoms are now classified as New/Worse or Baseline — only new symptoms count in correlation math. Four new Phase 2 charts show fluid intake bands vs. feeling by activity level, new symptom rates on active vs. sedentary days, sleep quality vs. next-morning BP, and late meal days vs. rough morning rate.
⚕️ Important — This is not medical advice

ClinBridge records your self-reported data and identifies patterns. It does not recommend specific fluid amounts, tell you whether to exceed your prescribed limit, or replace your care team's guidance. Use the patterns you collect to have a better-informed conversation with your cardiologist — not to make independent medical decisions.

Enabling / Disabling

Morning Check-In is on by default. To turn it off: Settings → Features → uncheck "🌅 Morning Check-In & Pattern Tracking." When off, no prompt appears and no data is collected. If you turn it back on, previously collected check-ins are still available and will appear in future reports.

FAQ

📱 Do I need to do anything when a new version is released?

Yes — always export your data before updating. Go to Device Sync & Backup → Export ALL Data and save the file. Then update, then import your data back. This takes about 60 seconds and protects everything you've recorded. The app will show you an update banner and walk you through the steps.

💾 How often should I back up my data?

At minimum, before any app update and once a week as a habit. Also back up before clearing your browser cache or before deleting the ClinBridge icon from your Home Screen — both of those actions erase your local data. Go to Device Sync & Backup → Export ALL Data.

📥 I imported my data but nothing appeared — what do I do?

After importing, the app reloads automatically. If your data still doesn't appear: close the app completely and reopen it. On any phone or tablet, close the app fully and reopen it. On any desktop or laptop browser, close the tab and open a fresh one at clinbridge.clinic. On iPhone/iPad specifically, swipe up from the bottom and swipe away ClinBridge before reopening. Your .json backup file is safe — you can import it again as many times as needed on any device.

🔄 Will my data transfer automatically when a new version releases?

Not automatically — you need to export before updating and import after. This is intentional: ClinBridge never moves your data without you taking a deliberate action. Your health data stays under your control at all times.

📊 What are the four Advanced Analytics detectors?

ClinBridge has four pattern detectors that analyze your historical data — not just today's readings. The HR Rate Detector finds sustained heart rate shifts and sudden changes. The Decompensation Warning monitors five clinical signs of CHF fluid overload building simultaneously. The Pulse Pressure Detector tracks the gap between your systolic and diastolic readings as a cardiac output indicator. The Symptom Convergence Detector finds clusters, escalations, and clinical patterns across your symptom history. All four are in the Analytics section of the main page.

📌 What is a Pinned Event and why should I use it?

When a detector finds a significant pattern, it suggests pinning it. A pinned event is permanently saved — it never disappears when your 90-day data window rolls forward. It captures the detector's finding, the event date, and all the raw data (BP readings, symptoms, weight, notes) from that day. Pinned events appear in your Doctor's Report as a dedicated section, in the 60-day Timeline as amber markers, and in the Pinned Events viewer under Analytics. Think of pins as your pre-prepared clinical evidence for your next cardiologist appointment.

🗂️ What should I do with pinned events after my cardiologist appointment?

After your appointment, open the Pinned Events viewer and tap "Archive & Clear." This permanently saves all current pins to an archive (you can always view them), then clears your active list so the next period starts fresh. ClinBridge will remind you automatically — if you have an upcoming appointment within 14 days, or if you just had one this week, a banner appears on the main page and inside the Pinned Events modal. If no appointment is logged but your oldest pin is 60+ days old, you'll see a gentle nudge to archive and refresh.

🔢 What does "math is directional, not definitive" mean?

It means ClinBridge's detectors can tell you that a pattern exists in your data — but they cannot tell you why it exists or what it means for your specific medical situation. A detected HR level shift is real math — but it could reflect a clinical change, a medication adjustment taking effect, seasonal variation, or something entirely benign. Your cardiologist provides the interpretation. ClinBridge provides the evidence and the pattern recognition to make that conversation richer and more productive than walking in with just a blood pressure number.

💾 How should I think about long-term data preservation?

ClinBridge keeps 90 days of rolling data on your device. For long-term preservation, export your data as a backup at the end of each quarter — the last day of March, June, September, and December. Save these files somewhere safe (iCloud, Google Drive, email to yourself). A new cardiologist years from now could import your Q3 2026 backup and see your complete cardiac picture from that period. Pinned events in each backup capture the most significant findings for that quarter, pre-annotated for clinical review.

🚨 A detector showed a red warning — should I go to the emergency room?

No — ClinBridge findings are not emergency indicators. A red finding means the pattern in your data is statistically significant and worth discussing with your cardiologist promptly — not that you are in immediate danger. If you are experiencing chest pain, severe shortness of breath, sudden dizziness, or other acute symptoms, call 911 or go to an emergency room regardless of what ClinBridge shows. ClinBridge is for pattern tracking over time, not acute symptom assessment.

About & Privacy

📌 New in v9.10.7 — April 3, 2026

  • 📋 Pinned Events — Communication Layer — Each pinned event now has two new sections. Log Communication: record who you communicated the finding to, the date, their response, and a status (🔴 Unresolved / 🟡 Deferred / 🟢 Addressed / 📋 Follow-up Ordered). Add Question: attach questions directly to the pin they belong to. In the appointment, read the pin aloud, then mark each question Asked (✓ checkbox) and log their response. Communication logs and questions travel with the pin into the archive — permanently preserved and always retrievable.

🚨 Fixed in v9.10.6 — April 3, 2026

  • 🔢 Numeric Field Scientific Notation Guard — All number input fields (BP systolic/diastolic, heart rate, fluid oz, weight, duration, and all others) now block the keys e, E, +, and −. Browsers treat these as valid scientific notation (e.g., 1e3 = 1000), allowing non-numeric characters to enter fields that should only accept whole numbers. Discovered when the optional fluid oz field in Log BP accepted the letter “e”. One global listener covers all 30+ numeric fields including future ones.

🐛 Fixed in v9.10.5 — April 3, 2026

  • 📋 All Notes Search — Single-Character Typing Bug Fixed — Typing in the All Notes search box was truncating input to a single character (manifested as only a lowercase “e” on ChromeOS in airplane mode). Root cause: every keystroke triggered a full modal rebuild via openAllNotesView(), which called showModal() and destroyed the search input element mid-typing. Fix: oninput now calls a new lightweight _filterNotesInPlace() function that only updates the notes list container — the search box element is never touched. Multi-character keywords now work correctly.

🚀 New in v9.10.4 — April 2, 2026

  • 📋 Help & About — Documentation Catch-Up — Known Issues and Planned Features tabs had not been updated since v9.9.x. All v9.10.0 through v9.10.3 releases are now documented in both tabs with full feature and fix summaries.
  • ✖️ Already-Linked BP Card — Dismiss Button — When the most recent BP reading is already paired with an activity, the gray “already linked” card in Log Activity now has a ✕ dismiss button so you can close it and proceed without being prompted.

🚀 New in v9.10.3 — April 2, 2026

  • 🩺 Fix — BP-Before Button in Manual Mode — The Take BP Before Activity button was invisible when Manual Entry duration mode was selected, because it lived inside the timerDisplay container. Moved outside that container so it is accessible in both Manual and Timer modes.
  • 📋 Manual Mode Info Card — When Manual Entry is selected, an amber info card now appears below the BP button explaining: (1) if you already took a BP before starting, tap Take BP Before Activity — it will pair correctly with your after reading; (2) if you skip it, the after-BP will still save but the session won't appear in BP change analysis which requires both readings. Card hides automatically when switching to Timer mode.
  • 📊 Recent BP Card at Activity Log Open — When Log Activity opens, the app checks your most recent BP reading and shows a contextual card. <30 min: green card with reading values, HR, time ago, and Use This Reading / Take New buttons. 30–60 min: amber card, same buttons, note that it's acceptable if you were resting. >60 min: gray card, no button — resting BP can shift meaningfully beyond 60 minutes. Already linked to another activity: gray info card, no button. No readings: no card shown.
  • 🔗 Use This Reading — Tagging Logic — Tapping Use This Reading does not copy the existing record. Instead it stores the reading's timestamp and at save time finds and stamps that record in the BP array with the new activityId and activityTiming:'before'. This preserves a single authoritative record rather than creating a duplicate.

🚀 New in v9.10.2 — April 2, 2026

  • 🩺 Symptom System — Full Overhaul — Cardiac Cough renamed to Congestive Cough throughout the app (condition lists and predefined symptoms). Headache (Morning) and Exertional Shortness of Breath consolidated to remove duplicates. Paroxysmal Nocturnal Dyspnea given its plain-language subtitle (Waking Breathless at Night). All 10 predefined symptoms and all 25 condition-specific symptom lists sorted alphabetically.
  • 📋 Manage Symptoms — Rebuilt in 3 Sections — Standard Symptoms (predefined, read-only reference list), Your Condition-Specific Symptoms (blue tappable cards showing which condition added each one plus a plain-language description of clinical significance — 21 descriptions written), and Your Custom Symptoms (with clear guidance to only add here if not already listed above).
  • 🔍 Fuzzy Symptom Matching — 70+ plain-language synonyms mapped to correct symptom names (e.g. "racing heart" → Palpitations, "can't breathe lying down" → Orthopnea). When adding or editing a symptom, the app checks for similar names and shows an amber "⚠️ Similar Symptoms Found" modal with plain-language descriptions and one-tap "This is what I meant" buttons. Prevents accidental duplicates without blocking legitimate custom entries.
  • 🔄 Bulk Rename in History — New "Rename in History" button in Manage Symptoms. Select any symptom name from your historical logs (with entry count shown), type the new name, and the app renames it across all stored readings in place. Detector caches are cleared automatically. Use this to clean up old entries — e.g. rename legacy "Cardiac Cough" entries to "Congestive Cough".
  • 💬 Clinical Context Prompt During Logging — Eight symptom families defined (cough, breathlessness, fatigue, near-fainting, chest, swelling, dizziness, palpitations). When you log a symptom from a family you've used before under a different name, a "📋 Quick Context" modal appears asking: Same symptom, different name / The symptom has changed / Skip. Your answer is stored in the notes field and surfaces in the Doctor's Report.
  • 📝 Log Symptom Modal — 5 Improvements — (1) Recent Symptoms: your last 3 distinct symptoms shown as green pill buttons at the top — one tap fills the dropdown. (2) Live severity descriptor: tapping 1–10 shows a plain-language description in matching color (green/amber/red), now at full width in senior-readable 17px bold type. (3) Auto-check "Known symptom of my condition" fires when the selected symptom is in your condition profile. (4) "Add New Symptom…" removed from dropdown and replaced with a "Symptom not listed? → Manage Symptoms" link. (5) Field labels rewritten as plain English questions with explanations for new users.
  • 🐛 Fix — Custom Symptom Delete Button — Delete button in Manage Symptoms was silently failing. Root cause: a duplicate deleteCustomSymptom function defined later in the file was overriding the correct one; the override used confirm() (which browsers can suppress) and read from the wrong localStorage key. Duplicate renamed to _deleteCustomSymptomByName, restoring correct modal-based deletion.
  • 🐛 Fix — Decompensation Badge Count — Badge on the Decompensation Warning button was showing 0 on page load, only updating after the detector was opened. Fixed by running the full 5-signal analysis silently at startup (1200ms delay) to pre-populate the window._decompLastPoints cache so the badge renders correctly from first view.
  • 🐛 Fix — Pulse Pressure Detector Pin Suggestions — PP Detector was not generating pin suggestions because the status title strings had been updated (e.g. to "Chronically Narrow") but the pin injection function was still matching the old strings. Updated to match all current status titles: Chronically Narrow, Reduced Pulse Pressure, Narrow Pulse Pressure, Wide Pulse Pressure. 🚀 New in v9.9.27 — March 22, 2026

  • 🚨 Decompensation Warning System — Five-signal clinical monitoring system based on AHA/ACC heart failure guidelines. Signal 1: Weight gain (≥2 lbs/24hr or ≥5 lbs/7 days = red). Signal 2: Cardiac Output (HR + pulse pressure trend over 3-day windows). Signal 3: Symptom frequency and severity escalation. Signal 4: Consecutive fluid over-limit days. Signal 5: Notes keyword scan for decompensation-related language. Composite scoring: All Clear → Early Indicator (1 signal) → Monitor Closely (2+ signals) → Contact Cardiologist (2+ red signals).
  • 🩺 Pulse Pressure Detector — Tracks pulse pressure (systolic minus diastolic) as a cardiac output indicator. Detects chronic narrow baseline (labeled "Chronically Narrow — Your Stable Baseline" when stable across 30+ readings), narrowing trends, widening trends, and cross-references HR level shifts for clinical context. Normal range: 40–60 mmHg. Alerts use proportionate language — a stable chronic baseline is informational, not alarming.

🚀 New in v9.9.26 — March 18, 2026

  • 🐛 Critical Fix: All Main Page Panels — Today's Blood Pressure, Weight, Symptoms, Activities, Meals, Medicines — All data panels on the Main Page were showing empty / "None" instead of today's readings after a launch-day regression in v9.9.25. Root cause: a second getAllHistoricalData(startDate,endDate) function introduced for the analytics engine silently overrode the main-page getAllHistoricalData() function (JavaScript last-definition-wins hoisting). Any call that passed no arguments received the analytics version, which requires a date range — returning empty arrays for everything. The analytics function has been renamed getHistoricalDataRange() and all its callers updated, restoring the correct main-page function as the sole handler for no-argument history calls.
  • 🐛 Fix: "Edit Past Entries" Button (Weight) — Now Works — Tapping "✏️ Edit Past Entries" on the Weight card now correctly switches to All History mode and populates weight entries from all previous days. This was broken by the same getAllHistoricalData override above — switching to 'all' history mode called the broken function and returned no weight data.
  • 🐛 Fix: All History Mode — BP, Weight, Symptoms, Activities, Meals, Medicines — Switching from Today to All History using the date filter buttons now loads the full 90-day history correctly across all panels. Previously all panels showed empty in All History mode due to the same root cause.
  • 🐛 Fix: Doctor's Report and Analytics — Historical Data Restored — The Doctor's Report, HR Rate Detector, and Advanced Analytics sections that call getAllHistoricalData() with no arguments now correctly receive all 90 days of data. These were also broken by the function override.
  • 🗓️ Weight History — Jump-to-Date Picker — When viewing weight history (Edit Past Entries), a date picker now appears at the top of the list. Pick any date and the view scrolls directly to that entry with a brief highlight pulse — no manual scrolling through 90+ entries required.
  • ⚠️ Weight History — Automatic Outlier Flagging — Each historical weight entry is now compared against your 7-day trailing rolling average (requires ≥ 2 entries in the window). Entries that deviate 10–19 lbs receive a yellow ⚠️ banner ("Possible data entry error"); entries that deviate ≥ 20 lbs receive a red 🚨 banner ("Likely data entry error"). Thresholds are grounded in AHA/ACC heart failure guidelines: normal daily fluctuation is 2–4 lbs; 5 lbs/week is a clinical alert threshold; 10+ lbs in a rolling window is almost certainly a typo or unit error (e.g. entering 68 kg instead of 150 lbs). A summary count of flagged entries appears in the picker panel so you know immediately if anything needs review.
  • 🔧 Cache Buster Version Updated — Version gate corrected to v9.9.26 to ensure users always load the latest release on upgrade.

🚀 New in v9.9.23 — March 12, 2026

  • 📊 Anchor Date Investigation — 3-Stat Summary Bar on Every Chart — Each chart (Systolic BP, Diastolic BP, Heart Rate, Weight, Fluid Intake) now shows three context pills above the chart area: Prior to target date 14-day avg, On target date, and After target date 5-day avg. All the investigative insight that tooltips were supposed to deliver is now always visible at a glance — no tapping required, no cross-chart interference possible. The tooltip system has been removed entirely.
  • 🐛 Anchor Date Charts — Cross-Chart Tooltip Interference Removed — After multiple failed attempts to reliably confine tap-triggered tooltips to their own chart on iOS, the tooltip system has been retired and replaced with the always-visible 3-stat summary bar above. Charts are now fully passive (no tap events) — scroll and zoom remain the only interactions.
    • — The actual iOS bug identified and eliminated. On iOS with -webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch, writing element.scrollLeft programmatically moves the compositor layer visually but the DOM property reads back as 0 until the next compositor sync tick. Auto-scroll worked (charts opened centered on anchor) but when you tapped, the touch handler read scrollLeft = 0 and computed indices from the far-left of the canvas — showing February dates for a chart visually showing March. Fixed by caching the intended scroll position in a JS variable (scrollLeftCache) set at the same moment as scrollLeft and kept current via a scroll event listener for user-initiated pans. Both the touchend and desktop onClick handlers now use this cache instead of the unreliable DOM property.
  • 🐛 Anchor Date Charts — iOS Tap & Scroll Fix (Round 2) — Two separate iOS-specific bugs fixed. (1) Auto-scroll to anchor date was not working on iPhone because iOS hadn't finished painting the layout when scrollLeft was set — fixed by deferring with two staggered timeouts so the scroll fires after the real width is available. (2) Tapping a data point still showed wrong dates because Chart.js processes touch coordinates before our onClick handler runs, using broken iOS math inside scroll containers — fixed by attaching a raw touchend listener directly on the scroll container that computes the data index from scratch using scrollLeft, completely bypassing Chart.js coordinate detection.
  • 📍 Anchor Date Charts — Auto-Scroll to Anchor Date — Charts now open pre-scrolled so the anchor date is centered in the visible window. Previously charts opened at the far left (earliest date) requiring manual horizontal scroll to reach the investigation period — and tapping after scrolling showed wrong dates due to an iOS coordinate bug. Opening centered on the anchor date eliminates the need to scroll entirely.
  • 🐛 Anchor Date Charts — Scroll-Offset Tap Fix — Tapping a data point after scrolling the chart horizontally was showing the wrong date (e.g. showing Feb 25 when tapping a Mar 10 point). Root cause: iOS does not correctly report canvas position via getBoundingClientRect() inside horizontally scrollable containers, so Chart.js mapped the tap back to the wrong index. Fixed by manually computing the correct data index using the scroll container's scrollLeft offset, bypassing Chart.js coordinate detection entirely.
  • 🐛 Anchor Date Charts — Phantom Tooltip Fix — The Heart Rate chart (and others) was showing a stale tooltip from a previous investigation even when no data point was tapped. Root cause: Chart.js fires tooltip callbacks on scroll proximity on iOS, not just explicit taps. Fixed by restricting chart events to click-only so the tooltip can only appear from a deliberate tap, never from scrolling past.
  • ✏️ Next Event — Quick Edit Button — The Next Event banner on the Main Page now includes an Edit Event button directly on the card. Tap it to instantly open the event editor for that event — change the time, fluid goal, or reminder settings without navigating to Settings → Events. Only appears for scheduled daily events (not plan-only entries).
  • ⚙️ Settings Accordion — Auto-Scroll on Expand — Tapping a collapsed Settings section now smoothly scrolls its header to the top of the view after it opens, so the content is immediately visible. Previously the section expanded below the fold with no indication anything had happened — easy to miss entirely.
  • 🐛 Anchor Date Investigation — Chart Tooltip Cross-Fire Fixed — Tapping a data point on any Anchor Date chart (Systolic BP, Diastolic BP, Heart Rate, Weight, Fluid Intake) now shows only that chart's tooltip. Previously all 5 charts shared a single tooltip handler, so whichever chart fired last would hijack the visible tooltip — causing a tooltip to appear on a chart you never touched. Each chart now gets its own tooltip function created in a dedicated closure, with a canvas-identity guard that silently ignores calls from any other chart instance. All 5 charts work fully independently.
  • 👆 Advanced Analytics — Tap-to-Show Chart Tooltips — Tapping any data point in the Anchor Date Investigation charts (Systolic BP, Diastolic BP, Heart Rate, Weight, Fluid Intake) now shows a persistent tooltip with the exact date, value + unit, and delta above or below your 14-day baseline average. Tooltip stays visible until you tap elsewhere — no more squinting at the Y-axis to estimate values.
  • 📈 HR Level Shift Detection — New Pattern Type — HR Rate Detector now detects sustained regime changes: periods where your heart rate was stable at one level, then durably shifted to a new level over a span of days — the kind of pattern your cardiologist looks for but the old detector completely missed. The algorithm groups readings into daily averages, slides a split-point across your timeline, and flags the largest shift where both the before-window and after-window are internally stable (not just noisy scatter). Cards show before/after averages, standard deviation, shift magnitude, and the estimated onset date with a one-tap Investigate button. Requires 6+ days of readings with ≥8 bpm sustained difference between windows.
  • 🩺 All Doctor Appointments — Card Layout Fixed — Text in appointment cards was displaying in a very narrow column on iPhone. Root cause: Edit/Delete action buttons were in the same horizontal flex row as the details text, squeezing it. Actions moved to their own full-width row below the card content.
  • 🔢 Anchor Summary — Floating Point Rounding Fixed — BP and HR deviation values in the plain-language summary were displaying raw floating-point numbers (e.g. "3.0999999999999943 mmHg"). Now rounded to 1 decimal place.
  • 🔍 Anchor Date Investigation — Advanced Analytics — Pick any date to instantly see a focused 20-day window (14-day baseline → anchor day → 5-day response) with all metrics aligned on the same timeline. Stacked charts show Systolic BP, Diastolic BP, Heart Rate, Weight, and Fluid Intake, each with a dashed 14-day baseline average line for instant deviation spotting. An annotation timeline below shows medications, symptoms, meals, activities, notes, procedures, and Morning Check-In responses day by day. Auto-generated plain-language summary is one tap away from the clipboard for your doctor. Investigations can be saved by name and reloaded at any future appointment — a March investigation is fully available in August.
  • 🔔 Alert Chime Fixed — Chime was silently dropping when AudioContext was suspended (e.g. after phone had been idle). Now schedules tones inside AudioContext.resume().then() so they always play.
  • 📱 Notification Capability Accurately Documented — All in-app text corrected: iOS alerts fire while ClinBridge is open and on screen. Background/locked-screen alerts require a future server-push implementation.
  • ✅ Event Reminder Card — Per-Action Stubs (Fix #1) — Tapping an action button replaces only that button with a grayed ✅ Done stub while remaining actions stay active. Done — Dismiss and Save as Missed remain throughout.
  • 🔧 Service Worker + Manifest Deployed — sw.js and manifest.json now ship as companion files, laying groundwork for future server-push notifications.

⚠️ Medical Disclaimer: ClinBridge is not a medical device and is not a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always consult your healthcare provider for medical decisions.

Accuracy statement: All pattern detection in ClinBridge is statistical and based on self-reported data. Findings are directional, not definitive — they identify patterns worth discussing with your cardiologist, not conclusions about your medical condition. Results may be affected by data entry errors, device measurement variability, and individual clinical factors that the app cannot account for.

🗂️ Data Management

Use the tools below to clear your health data stored on this device. These actions cannot be undone.

🔄 Reset Today's Data

Removes only today's BP readings, symptoms, meals, activity, dismissed events, and daily plan. Your settings, medications, procedures, appointments, and all previous days are kept.

⚠️ Delete ALL Data on This Device

Permanently erases everything: all daily readings (every day), settings, medications, procedures, appointments, custom symptoms/activities, analytics notes, and reminders. The app will return to a fresh-install state.

💡 Tip: Use "Reset Today" if you entered test data and want a clean start for the day. Use "Delete All" only if you want to completely start over or before giving someone else this device.

💾 When to Back Up Your Data

Your data lives only on this device. Back up regularly so you never lose it.

  • Before every app update — always export your data before installing a new version
  • Before clearing browser cache — clearing Safari or Chrome data wipes ClinBridge data too
  • Before deleting the Home Screen icon — removing the icon erases all data on iOS
  • Weekly — as a general habit, export once a week for peace of mind

How to back up: Go to Device Sync & Backup → Export ALL Data. Save the .json file to your Files app, iCloud, or email it to yourself.

🔄 How to Update to a New Version

When a new version is available, the app will show a banner at the top. Follow these steps in order — skipping step 1 risks losing your data.

  1. Export your data first — Device Sync & Backup → Export ALL Data → save the file
  2. Tap the update banner and follow the instructions to open the new version
  3. Once the new version loads, go to Device Sync & Backup → Import All Data
  4. Select your saved .json file — your data will be restored
  5. Verify your readings and settings appear correctly before using the app

📥 If Your Imported Data Doesn't Appear

After importing, the app reloads automatically. If your data still doesn't appear:

  • Wait for the page to fully finish reloading before checking
  • If data is still missing, close the app completely and reopen it
  • On iPhone: swipe up from the bottom, swipe away ClinBridge, then reopen
  • On Chromebook: close the tab and open a fresh one at clinbridge.clinic
  • If data still doesn't appear, try the import again — your .json file is safe to re-use

🔔 OS Notifications — What Works & What Doesn't

ClinBridge uses a Service Worker to send banner notifications. Here's the honest picture:

  • ✅ Fires reliably — you opened ClinBridge within the last few hours
  • ✅ Fires reliably — phone awake / screen on
  • ⚠️ May miss — iOS put the PWA process to sleep overnight
  • ❌ Will not fire — browser tab (must be Home Screen install)

To enable: Install via Safari Share → "Add to Home Screen," then allow notifications when prompted. ClinBridge will re-schedule the next 7 days of event reminders every time you open the app.

⚠️ Back up your data before removing the icon — deleting the ClinBridge home screen icon erases all your data on that device. Use Device Sync & Backup → Export ALL Data first.

🌡️ Barometric Pressure Alerts

Barometric pressure drops correlate with PPH episode severity. ClinBridge will detect significant pressure changes and issue a proactive heads-up so you can adjust hydration and activity before symptoms occur.

✅ Pattern Intelligence — Shipped in v9.9.27–30

Four dedicated detectors now live: HR Rate Detector (level shifts + rapid changes), Decompensation Warning (5-signal AHA/ACC system), Pulse Pressure Detector (cardiac output trending), and Symptom Convergence (clusters, escalation, clinical triads). Plus: Pinned Events for permanent preservation, 60-day Timeline, Appointment Snapshot, and Archive & Clear workflow.

🔗 Caregiver / Family Sharing

Optional read-only access for a spouse, adult child, or caregiver to view your dashboard and receive alerts — without being able to edit your data. Peace of mind for the people who care about you.

📱 Native iPhone & Android Apps

Full native apps with reliable background notifications, HealthKit / Google Fit integration, Apple Watch complications, and wrist-tap logging. No browser required.

⌚ Wearable Integration

Auto-import heart rate and activity data from Apple Watch, Fitbit, and Garmin — so you are not re-entering data that your devices already captured.

🍽️ Meal Impact Analysis

Correlate meal logs with post-meal BP readings to identify which foods or meal sizes consistently trigger PPH episodes. Over time, builds a personal map of your dietary BP triggers.

🌙 Sleep & Recovery Tracking

Log sleep quality and duration. Poor sleep is a major driver of next-day BP irregularities and OSA complications. Correlating sleep quality with BP trends gives your doctor a fuller clinical picture.

📖 Glossary

Plain-language definitions for every clinical term and app phrase used in ClinBridge. If you see a word in the app and don't know what it means, it's here.

Blood Pressure (BP)

The force your heart uses to push blood through your arteries, measured in millimeters of mercury (mmHg). Expressed as two numbers: systolic (the top number — pressure when your heart beats) over diastolic (the bottom number — pressure when your heart rests between beats). Example: 120/80 mmHg. Normal range for most adults is below 130/80, but your cardiologist will give you a personal target that may differ.

Pulse Pressure (PP)

The difference between your systolic and diastolic readings. Example: if your BP is 118/85, your pulse pressure is 33 mmHg. Normal range is 40–60 mmHg. A narrow pulse pressure (below 40) can indicate the heart is working harder to push blood forward — a pattern seen in reduced cardiac output and certain valve conditions. A wide pulse pressure (above 60) may indicate arterial stiffness. Many cardiac patients have a chronically narrow PP that is their personal baseline — what matters is change from that baseline, not comparison to textbook normals.

Heart Rate (HR)

How many times your heart beats per minute (bpm). Normal resting range is 60–100 bpm. Below 60 is bradycardia (slow heart rate); above 100 is tachycardia (fast heart rate). Patients with pacemakers may have a lower set rate limit — your pacemaker clinic can tell you what range is expected for your device settings.

Bradycardia

A heart rate below 60 bpm. In ClinBridge, the HR Rate Detector flags readings below 50 bpm specifically, as this is below the range most pacemakers are programmed to allow. Bradycardia is normal for well-trained athletes and some medication effects (beta-blockers, for example, intentionally slow the heart rate). Context matters — discuss any persistent low readings with your cardiologist or device clinic.

HR Level Shift

A sustained change in your heart rate baseline — where your resting HR was consistently at one level, then durably shifted to a new level and stayed there. This is different from a single high or low reading. ClinBridge's HR Rate Detector identifies these shifts statistically by comparing before-and-after windows for stability. A level shift is clinically significant because it suggests something changed in your cardiac state — compensation, medication effect, disease progression, or recovery. Your cardiologist will want to know.

CHF (Congestive Heart Failure) / Heart Failure

A chronic condition where the heart doesn't pump blood as efficiently as it should. "Congestive" refers to fluid backing up into the lungs and body (edema). Heart failure doesn't mean the heart has stopped — it means it's working harder than it should to maintain output. Management focuses on monitoring fluid balance, weight, symptoms, and medication adherence. ClinBridge's Decompensation Warning system is specifically designed to detect early signs of fluid buildup before symptoms become severe.

Decompensation

When a cardiac patient's condition worsens — typically due to fluid overload in CHF — to the point where symptoms become severe and hospitalization may be required. Early decompensation signs include rapid weight gain (fluid retention), worsening shortness of breath, swelling in legs and ankles, fatigue, and reduced activity tolerance. The goal of ClinBridge's Decompensation Warning detector is to surface multiple early signals before they progress to a crisis.

Signal Points (Decompensation Warning)

In the Decompensation Warning detector, each of the five clinical signals (weight, cardiac output, symptoms, fluid, notes) can score 0, 1, or 2 points based on severity. Maximum total is 8 points. The detector shows how many points are active and which signals contributed. One point alone is labeled "Early Indicator" — not alarming. Two or more points prompt closer monitoring. Two or more red-level signals prompt contacting your cardiologist.

Symptom Convergence

When multiple symptoms occur together or escalate simultaneously in a pattern that suggests an underlying common cause. In ClinBridge, convergence is detected across three layers: symptoms clustering within a 4-hour window on the same day, the same symptom worsening in severity over multiple days, and recognized clinical symptom triads. The significance is that individual symptoms are often dismissed — but a convergent pattern of multiple symptoms is harder to attribute to chance and more likely to represent a real clinical event.

Clinical Triad

A recognized combination of three symptoms that together suggest a specific condition or event. ClinBridge recognizes: the CHF Decompensation Triad (shortness of breath + fatigue + swelling/edema — a classic early decompensation pattern); the Arrhythmia Triad (palpitations + dizziness + chest pressure/tightness — may indicate an arrhythmia episode, note timing and duration); and the Systemic Symptom Pattern (nausea + fatigue + reduced appetite — nonspecific, worth noting but not alarming on its own). Triads are worth mentioning to your cardiologist, not reasons to panic.

PPH (Postprandial Hypotension)

A drop in blood pressure that occurs after eating. "Postprandial" means after a meal; "hypotension" means low blood pressure. Common in older adults and those with autonomic nervous system conditions. Typically defined as a drop of ≥20 mmHg systolic within 1–2 hours of eating. Symptoms include dizziness, lightheadedness, and fainting. ClinBridge's Post-Meal BP Patterns analysis in Advanced Analytics can help identify whether your BP drops consistently after meals.

Arrhythmia

An irregular heart rhythm — the heart beats too fast, too slow, or with an irregular pattern. Common types include atrial fibrillation (AFib), where the upper chambers quiver instead of beating regularly, and various bradycardias and tachycardias. Symptoms can include palpitations (feeling your heart beat irregularly or rapidly), dizziness, shortness of breath, or fatigue. Some arrhythmias are asymptomatic. ClinBridge logs heart rate with each BP reading; rapid changes and low readings are flagged for review.

90-Day Rolling Window

ClinBridge stores 90 days of daily readings on your device. After 90 days, the oldest day is removed as a new day is added — like a rolling 90-day window. This means data from more than 90 days ago is no longer in the app unless you exported a backup at that time. To preserve data long-term: export quarterly (last day of each quarter is a good practice). Pinned Events and Appointment Snapshots are exceptions — they are stored permanently and never roll off.

Pinned Event

A clinically significant finding that you've chosen to permanently preserve. When a detector flags something worth showing your cardiologist, tapping "📌 Pin" saves the finding, the date, and all raw data from that day to a permanent list that never rolls off. Pinned events appear in your Doctor's Report and on the 60-day Timeline. After your cardiologist appointment, use "Archive & Clear" to save all current pins to a permanent archive and start fresh.

Baseline (in ClinBridge)

Your personal "normal" — the consistent pattern your readings follow when nothing unusual is happening. ClinBridge uses the word "baseline" in two contexts: (1) Your personal BP/HR baseline — the average range your readings cluster around, used as the reference point for detecting changes; and (2) Baseline symptoms in the Morning Check-In — symptoms you experience routinely (such as chronic ankle swelling after a procedure) that are part of your normal state, not new developments. Baseline symptoms are recorded for your doctor but excluded from pattern correlation calculations.

"Math is directional, not definitive"

ClinBridge's core accuracy principle. The detectors use real statistical methods on real data — but statistics identify patterns, not causes. A detected HR level shift is mathematically real. Whether it represents disease progression, a medication effect, recovery, or random variation requires clinical judgment that only your cardiologist can provide. ClinBridge points in a direction and gives you the evidence to have a productive conversation — it does not tell you what that pattern means for your specific medical situation.

Verification vs. Generation

ClinBridge's design philosophy. Many health apps generate advice or recommendations — telling you what to do. ClinBridge instead verifies patterns across multiple data streams before surfacing a finding. It only escalates when signals converge — when two or more independent data streams agree that something changed. A single reading doesn't trigger an alert. A single signal point doesn't trigger a pin suggestion. This "verification first" approach is designed to prevent false alarms and preserve the credibility of findings that do get surfaced.
